title: Trigonometry: Compound and Double Angle Identities
seo_title: Grade 12 Compound and Double Angles Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Compound angle identities: cos(α ± β) = cos α cos β ∓ sin α sin β; sin(α ± β) = sin α cos β ± cos α sin β; double angle identities: sin 2α = 2 sin α cos α; cos 2α = cos² α − sin² α = 2cos² α − 1 = 1 − 2sin² α.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 12 trigonometry worksheets: compound angle and double angle identities, exact values and simplifying. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: cos(α + β) = cos α cos β − sin α sin β.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • sin(α ± β) = sin α cos β ± cos α sin β.
  • cos(α ± β) = cos α cos β ∓ sin α sin β (the sign changes).
  • sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ; cos 2θ = cos² θ − sin² θ = 2cos² θ − 1 = 1 − 2sin² θ.
  • Write angles like 75° as 45° + 30° to use special angles.

Examples

Example

cos 15°

cos(45° − 30°)

= cos 45° cos 30° + sin 45° sin 30°

Answer: (√6 + √2)/4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Splittingsin(α + β) ≠ sin α + sin β.
The signcos(α + β) has a minus.

items.q: A point moves along the curve x = 4 cos t, y = 6 sin t. Which equation describes the curve?
items.e: cos t = x/4 and sin t = y/6, and cos² t + sin² t = 1, so x²/16 + y²/36 = 1.

items.q: A point moves along the curve x = 5 cos t, y = 5 sin t. Which equation describes the curve?
items.e: x² + y² = 25(cos² t + sin² t) = 25. It is a circle of radius 5. x² + y² = 25.
